summary_oneline: Per-spec usage attribution is not a missing store — two usage stores, a shared CostCalculator and the exact correlation key already ship; what is missing is one join key between them, price coverage (1.2%), a usage read on the codex stream, and an ingestor for the two CLI seats.

subscribes to AfterClientCallEvent and fans UsageRecords out to every configured AbstractLogger sink — the merged precedent for adding a usage consumer without forking the pipeline
the existing shared price engine: cost_usd(provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens) over six bundled JSON price files, returning None rather than guessing
the existing versioned price table — input_per_1m / output_per_1m / cached_input_per_1m / valid_from, with no cache-creation tier

the OTel gen_ai.client.* metric surface and the cardinality whitelist that forbids session_id/user_id labels; also where FEAT-228 added parrot.agent.name — the precedent for extending an attribution dimension
FEAT-710's single cost computation at the origin, plus the _emit_round boundary where raw_usage (the only surviving cache-token carrier) is passed through
the normalised three-counter usage object every provider funnels into — the boundary at which cache tokens are destroyed
the already-shipped per-attempt usage dataset carrying exactly the correlation key the source proposes, written to a main-checkout-resolved append-only JSONL, gated behind DEV_LOOP_CODER_TELEMETRY
already builds and streams `codex exec --json` but contains no usage extraction at all — the single highest-leverage gap, since codex is 60% of attempts
already maps Codex event-stream token fields onto CompletionUsage — the parser dispatchers/codex.py is missing
owns the caller-generated execution_id and a deterministic canonical-worktree-path -> execution_id map; the real, in-process join that a hook-based cwd heuristic would be approximating
the MCP execution boundary; every per-task coder_* tool already takes execution_id, so the correlation key is already threaded through the MCP surface

the 12-member Literal with no usage.* kind and an envelope with no worktree field; compute_event_id is the existing idempotency primitive, but it hashes ts so it cannot express (seat, source_ref) dedup
reduces only six issue.* kinds into wiki pages rows, silently ignores unknown kinds, and compacts only category='issue' without ever truncating events.jsonl
the whole ledger's only DDL is a two-column ledger_state cursor — there is no per-plane table facility for a usage plane to extend

the gate deciding whether a new event kind is published into the git-committed sdd/ledger/ — an explicit decision the source never makes for usage rows
the dedup rule the source quotes correctly, but whose key is (backend, model, task_id, attempt_uid, pattern) — it does not include execution_id and dedups on a semantic pattern, not a request id

fourteen properties, none of them current_task, task_id or attempt_uid — the file the source's hook join was designed to read does not carry the fields
the merged FEAT-710 goal 'Cost is computed exactly once per LLM call', and the recorded rejection of the in-process bridge in closed PR #1747
the completed precedent for this exact shape of change: extend the attribution dimension of existing cost/token metrics rather than build a new plane

constraints.statement: FEAT-710 (merged, PR #1772) established that cost is computed exactly once per LLM call, at the origin in clients/base.py, because three subscribers were each recomputing it; and PR #1747 was CLOSED for proposing a fourth in-process subscriber that recomputed cost and collided with parrot.observability.setup_telemetry.
constraints.implication: The source's `usage.priced` event — a second place that turns tokens into USD from its own price table — is the shape review has already rejected once. Any design must read the origin's cost_usd rather than re-derive it, and must say explicitly why it is not a fourth subscriber.

constraints.statement: UsageRecord carries NO user_id/session_id by documented PII contract, and MetricsSubscriber enforces a cardinality whitelist in which 'user_id, session_id, prompt/completion content NEVER' appear as metric labels.
constraints.implication: A plane keyed on session_id/agent_id with per-spec Grafana panels violates both the privacy contract and the cardinality rule. feat_id/task_id are bounded and acceptable as labels; session_id is not.

constraints.statement: The ledger has no per-plane tables — its only DDL is a two-column ledger_state cursor; index.py contains no CREATE TABLE; compact() is hard-scoped to category='issue' and never truncates events.jsonl; LedgerLog.append caps each event at 4 KiB and the index replays from a byte cursor.
constraints.implication: 'Reuse the ledger and inherit export_snapshot/compact/audit for free' is false on every count. Per-request usage rows in that log is an unbounded-growth design on a structure with no rollup facility and no table to index into.

constraints.statement: LedgerService's entire public API is issue-shaped and offers no generic register-a-plane seam; a new event kind is a three-part change (Literal member + payload model + index reducer), and unknown kinds are silently ignored by the reducer.
constraints.implication: Adding usage.* to the Literal without a reducer would be accepted by the log and invisible to the index — a silent-failure mode. The ledger work is larger than the source's 'extend' estimate.

constraints.statement: The sdd-coder correlation key already exists and is already threaded through the MCP boundary: every per-task coder_* tool takes execution_id, and the engine owns a deterministic canonical-worktree-path -> execution_id map.
constraints.implication: For the dev-loop seat the join is an in-process lookup, not an inference. A hook-based cwd -> feat_id heuristic would be a weaker reconstruction of something the engine already knows exactly.

constraints.statement: execution_id was retrofitted by FEAT-559 and is documented 'Empty for historical records' — 332 of 1090 existing attempt rows have none; coder_end_execution additionally has an open defect (issue:cc372f700a47) making it an unreliable settlement signal.
constraints.implication: execution_id must be optional in any schema, and coder_end_execution is not yet a trustworthy place to emit a per-execution total.

constraints.statement: Cache tokens are destroyed at the client normalisation boundary: CompletionUsage is a three-counter model, a grep for cache_read/cache_creation/cached_input across parrot/clients/ returns nothing, and ClientRoundEvent.raw_usage is the only surviving provider-native payload.
constraints.implication: A four-counter cost model cannot be built from the normalised path. It requires widening CompletionUsage (or reading raw_usage per provider), and it touches three layers — price table, budget models, telemetry row.

constraints.statement: No price file has a cache-creation/cache-write tier (tier keys across all six files are exactly input_per_1m, output_per_1m, cached_input_per_1m, valid_from, note), the oldest table is 165 days stale against its own 90-day warning, and only 13 of 1090 recorded attempt rows (1.2%) use a priced model.
constraints.implication: Cost coverage, not cost machinery, is the binding constraint on 'what did FEAT-123 cost?'. Without a price-table refresh plus local/self-hosted model entries, 98.8% of real attempts price to None.

constraints.statement: wikitoolkit CLI warm start is measured at p50 ~415-425 ms (issue:f0a40d0853f2), against the source's own S2 pass criterion of < 150 ms per sub-agent stop.
constraints.implication: The `SubagentStop -> wikitoolkit usage bind` hook design is falsified as written by an existing measurement. A binding path must either be in-process, append directly to a file, or be batched.

constraints.statement: Claude Code telemetry is not enabled in this repository: .claude/settings.json sets only CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS and registers a single PreToolUse hook; no CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and no OTEL_* variables exist anywhere in it.
constraints.implication: The source's premise that Claude Code usage 'leaves through the OpenTelemetry plugin straight to Grafana' is not true here. Option A is not a zero-cost complement — the pipeline has to be turned on first, which is an ops and prompt-privacy decision.

constraints.statement: Official Claude Code documentation does not state whether a sub-agent's claude_code.api_request carries the parent session.id, nor whether prompt.id appears on sub-agent events, nor what query_source=auxiliary covers; but CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is documented in Bash, hook and stdio MCP server subprocesses.
constraints.implication: Spike S1 remains a real gate and its declared fallback is undocumented too, so S1 failing leaves no fallback standing. Conversely the stdio-MCP env var means the parrot-sdd-coder server can read the orchestrating session id itself, without a hook.

constraints.statement: 'Seat' already has at least two incompatible meanings in this codebase — the sdd-coder roster seat (label 'a'/'b'/'c' plus kind and backend) and the observability seat (a free accounting string such as 'development.w1') — and the source introduces a third.
constraints.implication: Any schema must pick one vocabulary and declare the mapping for the other two, or reports will silently mix dimensions.

constraints.statement: A new usage.* kind must declare itself in shared_log.is_shareable; the committed sdd/ledger/ log is git-tracked and synced by hooks.
constraints.implication: Sharing usage events puts per-attempt token counts into git history for every machine; not sharing them makes the plane per-machine, which defeats the 'one usage plane' goal for a team. The source makes neither choice.

constraints.statement: FEAT-228 (per-agent cost/usage metrics) is complete — 6/6 tasks done, closed 2026-06-08 — and its parrot.agent.name label is live in metrics.py in ten places.
constraints.implication: There is a successful, merged precedent for exactly this shape of change: widen the attribution dimension of the existing metrics rather than build a parallel store. FEAT-783 is the next dimension on the same axis.

constraints.statement: TASK-4381 (HelixLedgerStore + LedgerService backend dispatch, FEAT-670) is active, and sdd_coder/engine.py is the package's hottest file with open encapsulation defects at begin_execution/suspend_model.
constraints.implication: A new ledger plane must dispatch through LedgerService rather than bind SQLite directly, and an ingestor at the execution boundary lands on contended, actively-churning ground.

enrichment.scope_statement: Make per-spec usage and cost answerable by extending the attribution dimension of the usage pipeline that already exists, closing the codex usage gap, and fixing price coverage — rather than by building a new ledger-owned usage plane, which the research contradicts on five independent counts.
new: A usage read on the codex event stream: dispatchers/codex.py already streams `codex exec --json` and never looks for tokens; OpenAICodexClient._usage_from_event already knows how to parse them. Highest leverage single change — the codex seat is 60% of attempts and 0.0006% of recorded tokens.

Per-spec attribution ContextVars (current_feat_id / current_task_id / current_attempt_uid / current_execution_id) beside the existing current_run_id / current_seat, set by the sdd-coder engine, which already owns all four values.
One AbstractLogger sink that persists attributed UsageRecords durably, following the run_ledger.py precedent (append-only, never merge, so retries do not overwrite each other).

A cache-creation / cache-write price tier in observability/cost/pricing/*.json, plus entries for the models actually run (gpt-5.6-terra, zai.glm-4.7-flash, qwen, minimax, mistral.devstral) and the Claude 5 family.
A reader: `wikitoolkit usage report --feat FEAT-NNN [--by task|seat|model]` plus the paired MCP tool, following the TASK-4020 CLI+MCP-in-one-task pattern.
For the two CLI seats only: an OTLP ingestor. Codex speaks gen_ai.usage.* natively and so can share parrot's own schema; Claude Code's claude_code.* names do not, so it is the odd one out.

add the new attribution labels under the cardinality whitelist, exactly as FEAT-228 added parrot.agent.name
widen CompletionUsage to carry cache_read / cache_creation (and consider Codex's reasoning_output_tokens), since the normalised path currently destroys them
add cache counters and a cost field to AttemptUsageRow, or retire it in favour of the observability sink — today the repo has two parallel usage datasets with no shared key
read usage from the JSON event stream it already parses; the natural home is dispatchers/_shared.py, since twelve sibling dispatchers have the same gap
refresh (oldest is 165 days stale), add the cache-creation tier, add the self-hosted and current-generation models

untouched: knowledge/wiki/ledger/ — no usage.* event kind, no usage plane, no new DDL. The ledger has no plane tables, its compact() is issue-scoped, its log caps events at 4 KiB and never truncates, and a second backend (HelixLedgerStore, TASK-4381) is in flight.
clients/base.py cost computation — FEAT-710's G5 stands: cost is computed once at the origin and read, never recomputed by a consumer.
memory/compaction report_usage — implemented but a prompt-token calibration hook keyed by (user_id, session_id, chatbot_id); it never fires for coder attempts, Claude Code or Codex.
The existing Grafana/OTel session-level dashboards and the FEAT-774 BigQuery sink landing upstream in navigator-eventbus.
A new usage/prices.yaml — a second price table would create two sources of truth for the same number.

patterns_to_follow.pattern: FEAT-228: widen the attribution dimension of existing metrics (it added parrot.agent.name and shipped complete, 6/6 tasks, 2026-06-08)
FEAT-479 run_ledger.py: an append-only AbstractLogger sink that is a SINK, not an EventProvider — the existing subscriber owns the subscription

FEAT-554 telemetry.py: durable root resolved via git-common-dir to the main checkout and REFUSED inside a worktree, fail-open writes that never change a dispatch outcome, per-event size cap, path-traversal guard on the id
TASK-4020: ship the CLI subcommand and its MCP tool in one task

integration_risks: Being a fourth consumer of AfterClientCallEvent is precisely what closed PR #1747. The design must ride the existing UsageRecordingSubscriber fan-out as a sink, not add a subscriber.

Two usage datasets already exist with disjoint keys (observability run_id/seat/node_id/cycle vs sdd-coder feature_id/task_id/attempt_uid/execution_id). Shipping a third without retiring or joining one of them makes the original problem worse.
Both CLI seats are outside AbstractClient entirely and neither exports telemetry today; turning Claude Code's on carries prompt-content privacy implications that are an ops decision, not a code one.

Attributing cost to abandoned attempts (which the source correctly wants) interacts with issue:c4d0e7a028ca — codex sdd-coder seats can never commit, so codex attempts are routinely abandoned; their cost is real and must not be dropped.
cumulative_cost_usd on UsageRecord is process-cumulative, so an sdd-worker process outliving several tasks yields a monotonically rising number that must never be summed per task.
sdd_coder/engine.py is the package's hottest file with open defects at the exact boundary (issue:cc372f700a47, issue:700660c7f663).
